messages.subject: Standard errors
parts:
I obtained standard errors in an IRT-graded response model. Are there guidelines for acceptable standard errors in the discrimination parameters and the threshold parameters? Are the sample size and the level of the discrimination parameter relevant? For example, I conducted a preliminary study that, among other measures, included a brief, validated measure. The sample size after na.omit was 310.  All discrimination parameters were above 1, most in the range of 2-3.  ICCs were good.  SEs for discrimination parameters ranged between .18 and .39.  What can be concluded regarding the discrimination parameters?  SEs for threshold parameters were around .10.  Thanks in advance.

Robert Semel

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Standard errors
parts:
Hi Robert,

No doubt someone has made recommendations regarding the magnitude of SEs, though I'm not sure how much value they would be in practice. You could use SEs for hypothesis testing purposes w.r.t. whether a new item should be included in a test battery, but in general I would advise against that as there are more important issues in that context than whether a discrimination is "significant" in the conventional sense. Mainly, I would use the SE information to help safeguard against over interpretation of a test item's discrimination capabilities as large SEs result in wide CIs, so an ostensibly large discrimination could simply be due to sampling uncertainty, and it's worthwhile to know that. HTH.

Phil
